title: [D7 Emit] At-least-once emission of every terminal outcome, counted engine-side
summary: `helena.sink.emit` produces one message per terminal outcome to `HELENA_OUTPUT_TOPIC` through `helena.broker` — `normal` verdicts, `suspicious` ones and typed failures alike, an escalated context once under the analyst's identifier carrying the triage decision beside it — and returns `EmissionCounts`, reconciling what the broker acknowledged against `helena_analytical_emission_counts`, the plain view `sql/migrations/0020` adds so an operator can ask the engine the same number in plain SQL after the broker has discarded everything. `scripts/emit.py` is the operator surface, `docs/decisions/0037-at-least-once-emission.md` §2 the deduplication contract and §4 the measured output-volume hazard, `docs/runbook.md` §12 the runbook.
assumption_validated: Two, both measured rather than reasoned about. (1) THE AT-LEAST-ONCE CONTRACT IS IMPLEMENTABLE WITH NO EMISSION STATE AT ALL, and the duplicate it produces is deduplicable: emitting twice puts two messages on the topic whose bytes are byte-for-byte identical and whose `assessment_id` — in the payload and in the `helena-assessment-id` header — is one key, executed against the pinned blink in `test_emitting_twice_repeats_the_key_rather_than_minting_a_new_one`. The design pressure this answers is real: a sequence number, an emission timestamp or a delivery id would each have satisfied 'at-least-once' and left a consumer two messages it could not tell were one. (2) THE ENGINE-SIDE COUNT SURVIVES WHAT THE BROKER DOES NOT. Three messages emitted, the topic drained, and the engine still answers 3 while a tenant that has assessed nothing answers 0 — the two readings `concept/03` says must be distinguishable. Also measured, because the ADR needed a number rather than an adjective: one message over the ten-record layers capture (one host, one five-minute window, 41 entities, one source) is 36 994 bytes and 41 rows of the sink view.
makes_buildable: Task 48 (metrics and reconciliation) gets `helena_analytical_emission_counts` as the 'emitted rows' term of its reconciliation view, already at message grain and already joined to tenant and sensor, and `scripts/emit.py --count` as the shape a `helena status` subcommand can follow. Task 49 (the conformance suite) gets two executed rows of the must-never-happen table it can point at rather than re-derive: 'a budget-truncated run returning normal' has its egress half here (a `normal` is emitted, not filtered at the transport), and 'a typed failure becoming something else' has `outcome_kind = typed_failure` with a null verdict on the wire. Task 51 (secrets hygiene) gets the actual bytes on a topic to assert over, not just `OutputMessage`. Task 52 (end to end) gets the last stage: ingest -> context -> enrich -> triage -> analyse -> `uv run scripts/emit.py`, with a drain that needs no consumer to be observable.

verification.detail: 1709 passed, 1 skipped in 660 s, full suite, against a pinned RisingWave 3.0.3 and a pinned blink 0.2.0 started by the session fixtures. The skip is tests/test_analyst.py:1725, which skips itself when the configured model endpoint returns a typed failure — it did (`timed_out`) on this run and it is nothing to do with this increment; an earlier full run in this session had it passing. tests/test_sink.py is 34 tests (23 from task 46, 11 new); eight of the new ones go over the real wire — they emit through `helena.broker` to the pinned broker and drain the topic back with a real consumer, and every assertion is about what came off it rather than about what `emit` returned. Covered by execution: three terminal outcomes on one topic (a `normal` verdict, a typed failure and an escalated pass) with the triage half of the escalated pass absent; the escalated message carrying the analyst's classification and the triage decision; the bytes parsing back into a model equal to `SinkStore.project`; both headers; two emissions producing identical bytes under one key; the engine still counting 3 after the topic was drained while another tenant counts 0; another deployment's assessments not emitted; the counter view and `SinkStore.pending` agreeing with plain SQL; `EmissionCounts` refusing emitted > pending and reporting emitted < pending; and an unnamed topic refused before anything is produced. `scripts/emit.py` was also run by hand against the live dev engine and broker in both modes (`--count` on an empty store, and a real drain that created the topic and flushed). `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` and `uv lock --check` both clean. No new dependency, so uv.lock is unchanged. TWO FAILURES ON THE FIRST FULL RUN, both fixed and both reported here rather than left in a footnote: `tests/test_enriched.py::test_the_enriched_context_is_the_first_analytical_object` pins the list of analytical objects that read something and my counter view is a third entry (a correct test, updated); `tests/test_assessment_replay.py::test_the_column_list_is_the_one_the_engine_holds` queried `information_schema.columns` without a `table_schema = current_schema()` filter and saw the dev store's `public` schema as well as the test schema (the defect task 46 recorded as a lesson; now fixed rather than only noted).

escalations.detail: `HELENA_OUTPUT_TOPIC` is a new required variable, with `Infrastructure.output_topic` beside `ingest_topic` and an entry in `.env.example`. Not a decision that needed asking — `helena/config.py` already carried the comment that the output topic 'enters with the sink that writes to it', and this is that sink — but it is recorded because it is a new required variable and a deployment that does not set it now fails at startup. Nineteen test modules gained the line in their ENVIRONMENT dict, which is mechanical. It also comes with a refusal: `Infrastructure` rejects a configuration where the two topic names are equal, because the pipeline would consume its own output as flow records, quarantine every one, reconcile every counter, and present as a sensor sending malformed traffic.

`0019_sink.sql`'s `Read by:` was edited to name `helena_analytical_emission_counts`, which tests/test_view_layering.py requires of every relation that is read. The checksum ledger is over the bytes, so a store migrated before 0020 must be dropped and re-migrated. Same standing cost as the four earlier retrofits; docs/runbook.md §5 now names this one in that list.

tests/test_assessment_replay.py::test_the_column_list_is_the_one_the_engine_holds gained a `table_schema = current_schema()` filter. It is not this increment's code, but this increment's verification is what hit it, it is a defect task 46 already recorded and did not fix, and leaving it means the next session rediscovers it. Roughly thirty other unscoped `information_schema` queries exist across the suite; only this one builds an ORDERED LIST from the result, which is why only it fails — the others compare sets or dicts and are merely fragile. Not swept, deliberately: a thirty-call-site change in a task about emission would bury the increment.

deferred: A CONTINUOUS EMITTER. `emit` is a DRAIN with no cursor: it reads every terminal outcome the store holds, produces it, and returns. There is no streaming job and nothing runs on a schedule, because the sink view cannot be the source of one (ADR-0036 §2's measurement: the enriched context derives `status` from `now()`, which a streaming query rejects). So a message reaches the topic when somebody runs `scripts/emit.py`, and running it twice re-emits everything. That is the at-least-once contract at prototype scale and it is also the thing that would have to change first at real rates.

ANY RECORD OF WHAT WAS EMITTED. No ledger table, no cursor, no delivery receipt. Considered and rejected in ADR-0037 §3 for three reasons: it would make the sink write to the store it exists to read from; its only use is suppressing a duplicate the contract says the consumer removes; and it is the first step toward the exactly-once `concept/03` says is not attempted — the row would be written after the produce, so a crash between them trades a duplicate the consumer handles for a loss nothing detects.

THE OUTPUT-VOLUME HAZARD ITSELF. Recorded with a measurement (ADR-0037 §4: one message over the smallest realistic context is 36 994 bytes, the topic carries the context rate and not the alert rate, and the drain has no cursor so a second run doubles it) and NOT solved. No filter, no sampling, no compaction, no retention policy. A filter that dropped `normal` at the edge would re-implement triage in the transport, which is `concept/07`'s must-never-happen table arriving by a different route. Revisiting needs a measured message rate against a real capture — `concept/08`'s open question.

ANY CONSUMER. Nothing outside this repository has read one of these messages and no schema has been negotiated with anything. `helena.sink`'s maturity label is `experimental` and says so. 'Replacing the broker is a configuration change' is still a property of the code's shape on the egress side as it is on the ingress side: it has run against blink 0.2.0 and against no other broker.

A KAFKA MESSAGE KEY. Messages are produced with headers and no key. The broker runs one partition, so a key would order nothing and compact nothing; it would be machinery for a case that does not exist. The deduplication key is a header and a payload field, which is where a consumer can actually use it.

THE FOUR THINGS TASK 46 LEFT UNOWNED, all unchanged: the escalation record's `thresholds_version` reaches no row; the composition rule's decision and proposed claims are not stored so `classification` is what the model said; no redaction is performed in the sink; and `context_resolved = FALSE` still cannot tell 'the context was evicted' from 'the context version moved on'.
lessons: A `normal` TRIAGE RESULT CANNOT CARRY CITATIONS, and the contract enforces it: `AgentResult(classification='normal', citations=(...))` raises `a 'normal' triage decision returns verdict and confidence only (concept/04)`. That makes the `normal` message the one with the least in it, which is also why it is the one an emitter would be tempted to drop — so it is the first of the three outcomes in the emission test.

THE PINNED BROKER'S RECLAIM IS NOT INSTANT AND A TEST THAT ASSERTS AN EMPTY TOPIC IMMEDIATELY AFTER A DRAIN FAILS. Measured again here (it cost one red test): a second drain started right after the first still returned all three messages. tests/test_broker.py already measures this properly with a 45-second deadline and a control topic; anything else should assert on the ENGINE-side consequence rather than re-measure the broker.

AN `information_schema` QUERY IN A TEST MUST FILTER ON `table_schema = current_schema()`. Only one engine runs per machine, so a migrated dev store in `public` sits beside every test schema, and a query that builds an ordered LIST from an unfiltered result silently concatenates the two. This is the second session to hit it (task 46 recorded it; this one fixed the call site that fails). Running `scripts/migrate.py` against the dev store mid-session — which is what verifying an operator script requires — is enough to create the condition.

THE ENGINE-SIDE COUNT BELONGS IN A MIGRATION, NOT IN A PYTHON QUERY, and the reason is in what the count is for. The situation it answers is 'the consumer sees nothing and the broker has discarded everything', which is a situation where the operator is not running the emitter. A count that only exists as a method on `SinkStore` requires running Python to ask; `SELECT * FROM helena_analytical_emission_counts` does not. This is the same shape as `helena_ingest_counts` in 0004 and for the same reason.

READ THE LIST BEFORE THE COUNT, NOT AFTER. Both are reads of a store still being written to, and a pass landing between them has to fall on the side the counters can describe. List-then-count makes it raise `pending` — reported as 'run it again'. Count-then-list makes it raise `emitted` above `pending` and be refused as a double-emission that never happened.

`count(DISTINCT ...)` AND `GROUP BY` OVER THE SINK VIEW WORK IN A BATCH VIEW ON RISINGWAVE 3.0.3, which is not obvious given that the same view cannot be the source of a streaming job at all. The counter view is plain and is only ever read in batch; it could not be materialized even if that were wanted, for the reason 0019's head records.
failed_approaches: A `CREATE SINK` FROM THE SINK VIEW TO THE OUTPUT TOPIC — the task's first step, as written. Not attempted, because task 46 already measured that it cannot be bound: `helena_analytical_enriched_context` derives `status` from `now()` and RisingWave 3.0.3 rejects `now()` outside a WHERE clause in a streaming query, so nothing downstream of it can be a streaming source (ADR-0036 §2). What was built instead satisfies the step's actual requirement — a sink from the sink view to the output topic over the Kafka wire protocol, addressed by configuration only — with `helena.broker` as the one Kafka client in the repository, which is what keeps `concept/instruction.md` §2's 'the broker is addressed only through the Kafka wire protocol, on both ends' true with one mechanism rather than two.

AN EMISSION LEDGER TABLE, so that a re-run would emit only what had not been emitted. Rejected before it was written, and the argument is in ADR-0037 §3 so nobody has to re-derive it: it makes the sink write, its only use is suppressing a duplicate the consumer is contractually required to remove, and the obvious next step (skip what is in the ledger) converts a duplicate the consumer handles into a loss nothing detects, because the row is written after the produce.

A SECOND DRAIN ASSERTING THE TOPIC IS EMPTY as the proof that the broker keeps nothing. Written, run, and failed — the reclaim lands seconds later, which tests/test_broker.py already measures. Replaced with the assertion that actually belongs in this file: after the topic has been drained once, the ENGINE still answers 3.

`pending` READ BEFORE `terminal()`. Written that way first. Reversed once the failure mode was traced: a pass landing between the two reads would make `emitted` exceed `pending` and be refused as a double-emission, which is the one thing `EmissionCounts` is supposed to catch for real.
next_session_should_know: Emission exists and the D7 pair is complete. NINE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `sink.emit(store=SinkStore(...), producer=BrokerProducer.from_settings(settings), topic=settings.infrastructure.output_topic) -> EmissionCounts(pending, emitted)`, and `scripts/emit.py` is the operator wrapper (`--count` asks the engine and produces nothing). (2) `HELENA_OUTPUT_TOPIC` IS A NEW REQUIRED VARIABLE. If you add a test module with its own ENVIRONMENT dict, it needs the line or `Settings.load` fails naming it — and it may not equal `HELENA_INGEST_TOPIC`, which startup refuses. (3) THE ENGINE-SIDE COUNT IS `helena_analytical_emission_counts` (sql/migrations/0020), one plain view, `count(DISTINCT assessment_id)` grouped by tenant and sensor. Task 48's reconciliation view should join it rather than recount the sink view — the sink view's grain is 41 rows per message on the layers capture. (4) 0019 WAS RETROFITTED AGAIN (`Read by:`), so a store migrated before 0020 must be dropped and re-migrated; docs/runbook.md §5 lists it. (5) IF YOU RUN `scripts/migrate.py` AGAINST THE DEV STORE TO VERIFY SOMETHING BY HAND, the `public` schema then sits beside every test schema and any unfiltered `information_schema` query in the suite sees both. One call site was fixed here; about thirty others are unfiltered and merely fragile because they compare sets rather than lists. Add `table_schema = current_schema()` to any new one. (6) THE DEDUPLICATION CONTRACT IS ADR-0037 §2 and it is what you hand a consumer: deduplicate on `assessment_id` (payload field and `helena-assessment-id` header), expect `normal` and typed failures, do not infer ordering from arrival, check `message_version` first. (7) EMISSION IS A DRAIN WITH NO CURSOR AND NOTHING RECORDS WHAT WAS EMITTED. Running it twice re-emits everything, on purpose. If a later task wants 'emit only what is new', read ADR-0037 §3 first — that change is not the small one it looks like. (8) THE OUTPUT-VOLUME HAZARD IS RECORDED WITH A MEASUREMENT AND NOT SOLVED (ADR-0037 §4, 36 994 bytes for the smallest realistic message). Do not add a filter, a sampler or a retention policy without treating it as the decision it is; filtering `normal` at the transport is `concept/07`'s must-never-happen table arriving sideways. (9) TASK 49's CONFORMANCE SUITE CAN NOW ASSERT OVER REAL BYTES ON A REAL TOPIC — `tests/test_sink.py`'s `drain` and `emitted` helpers are three lines each and are the pattern.
